shortened: And likewise I have detached Myself from these who follow the desires of their souls and are not conscious in any matter, and whose only concern in this world is to put themselves before God's servants and to sit in the chief seats of gatherings and to boast and make claims about that which they neither know nor understand.

order.why: Keep the reported warning concerning office used for personal interests.
shortened: If the object, however, is to promote personal interests, then such a position will be injurious to humanity and not beneficial to the public.

order.why: Read the reported criticism of named individuals as a particular historical judgment.
Keep the reported complaint about visitors in its setting.
Read the reported criticism of political parties’ private aims.
Consider the reported loss of prosperity through competing private ends.
Keep the charge that another person is being used for private purposes.
shortened: Never was their purpose the branch, nor is it now. Rather, they have made him a means for attracting people to their own causes.

order.why: Read the danger of attributing selfish conduct to the divine Cause.
Contrast private material interests with the common good.
shortened: Today, all the peoples of the world are indulging in self-interest and exert the utmost effort and endeavor to promote their own material interests. They are worshipping themselves and not the divine reality, nor the world of mankind. They seek diligently their own benefit and not the common weal.

order.why: Hear the reported question about a life limited to private advantage.
shortened: Then what value can be placed on these souls who desire nothing except the promotion of their own interests and advantages?

order.why: Read the reported futility of selfish ends.
Consider the reported account of pleasure that scatters attention.
shortened: Some may imagine that because they frequent theaters, accumulate wealth, or attend balls, they are always enjoying life: whereas, in reality, these things often scatter thoughts, confuse the minds and dissipate the faculties. The effect of these amusements is like the effect of the wine upon the body:-it exhilarates at first, but its after effect leaves one weak and the mental faculties exhausted.

order.why: Read self-indulgence and fanaticism as obstacles to flourishing.
Keep the warning about the ungrateful self in its source form.
shortened: Such is the condition of people and the fruit of the whisperings of the ungrateful self. Vain indeed is that which they do! Soon thou shalt see them in evident loss.

order.why: Consider the reported mire of egoism.
shortened: It is because they are seeking their own interests and not the good-pleasure of the Lord of mankind. They are steeped in the quagmire of their own egoism and are not striving to save themselves out of the bog of selfishness and shake their bespattered bodies with soiled mud and dirt.

order.why: Read the reported danger of mistaking a narrow circle for universal sympathy.
shortened: Stiff-necked and self-willed they take their narrow circle of affected fellow-feeling as the limitless sea of universal sympathy or the tiny rivulet of their self-love as the fountain-head of an all-inclusive brotherhood.

order.why: Consider the reported cloud that hides inner light.
shortened: How often they let the cloud of self and ego becloud the horizon and thus prevent the stars of their divine verities from shinning!

order.why: Read the mirror turned from the Sun toward the wolf of desire.
Consider tests as cleansing the obstructing veil of self.
shortened: It is clear, then, that tests and trials are, for sanctified souls, but God's bounty and grace, while to the weak, they are a calamity, unexpected and sudden.

These tests, even as thou didst write, do but cleanse the spotting of self from off the mirror of the heart, till the Sun of Truth can cast its rays thereon; for there is no veil more obstructive than the self, and however tenuous that veil may be, at the last it will completely shut a person out, and deprive him of his portion of eternal grace.

order.why: Read the reported interpretation of Satan as the insistent self.
Examine the paradox of self-rule becoming bondage.
Hear the image of desire as intoxication.
shortened: The intoxication of selfish desire hath held men back from the Lord of all being.

order.why: Read the prayer concerning worship of one’s own desires.
Consider the choice between divine guidance and private prompting.
shortened: This Day they have cast away what is with God and taken what their own selves and desires have commanded them.

order.why: Hear the direct counsel concerning the promptings of self.
shortened: O My handmaidens! Follow not the promptings of self, but follow that which hath come by a clear command.

order.why: Turn toward release from bondage through remembrance.
shortened: Say: Deliver your souls, O people, from the bondage of self, and purify them from all attachment to anything besides Me. Remembrance of Me cleanseth all things from defilement, could ye but perceive it.

order.why: Read renunciation and trust in relation to peace.
shortened: There is no peace for thee save by renouncing thyself and turning unto Me; for it behooveth thee to glory in My name, not in thine own; to put thy trust in Me and not in thyself, since I desire to be loved alone and above all that is.

order.why: Hear the concise redirection of thought toward the Beloved.
Consider the reported contrast between attention to self and Truth.
Read the reported severance from egotism in the language of love.
shortened: By them, man is brought to the condition of severance from his egotism and being absorbed into the Ocean of Love Divine.

order.why: Hear the blessing upon one not kept back by self.
Connect words and deeds with bringing assurance to others.
Read the reported hope for justice and fairness in place of selfishness.
shortened: Perchance, God willing, they may become mindful and aware, be released from negligence, abandon tyranny and oppression, treat each other with justice and fairness, and give up the dictates of selfishness and personal interest.

order.why: Close the linked sequence with the reported vision of shared happiness under justice.
shortened: Therefore we must all live in the utmost of happiness and comfort under a just rule and regulation in accordance with the laws of God, because this life is fleeting, and if man looks after himself only, he is no better than the animal, for the animal alone is to that degree egotistic.

order.why: Retain the supplied warning about corrupted motives.
Close with the supplied invitation to improve one another’s lives.

questions: What does the story of the starving dog reveal about the difference between feeling love and acting upon it?
Which subtle forms of self-interest in these passages are hardest to recognize in oneself?
How can a concern for spiritual growth differ from the self-absorption the compilation criticizes?
What do the images of mirror, cloud, veil, and bondage each add to your understanding?
How does Luke’s parable invite examination of our own motives without becoming a reason to despise someone else?
What practical choices could connect freedom from selfishness with generosity and the betterment of others’ lives?

references.label: 1 · Luke 18:9–14 · Prayer and self-righteousness
references.note: The parable is addressed to those confident in their own righteousness who despise others. Compare the two prayers with the compilation’s warnings about subtle self-interest within religious life. The invitation is to examine one’s own posture and need for mercy; turning its figures into labels for other people would reproduce the problem the passage raises.
